{"body":"## Problem

The installed kc-dev-flow loader cannot resume a pinned stage after normal report additions, and its pin transition rule does not represent a validation-to-implementation correction. Spacedock already exposes `dispatch build --feedback-reflow`, but the required kc-dev-flow pin check blocks the handoff first.

This stops already-approved product repairs. Replacing the pin is not a sufficient fix: the next appended report recreates the mismatch.

## Evidence and versions

- Executed against kc-dev-flow 4.1.1, Python 3.13.2, macOS arm64, with Spacedock 0.27.2.
- The installed plugin version and contract digest match the preserved pin. The live work item differs from its pinned Git revision only by 327 appended lines of review, approval and diagnostic records; the original bytes were not edited.
- Read-only inspection of kc-dev-flow 4.3.0 at main commit `d75b92dade55ac6911d5bff8282497488a05a514` finds the same whole-document hash and forward-only transition conditions. That newer version was not executed or adopted in this diagnostic.
- Relevant source: [bind_stage_pin](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/d75b92dade55ac6911d5bff8282497488a05a514/kc-dev-flow/scripts/profile-contract-loader.py#L230), [whole-document hash](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/d75b92dade55ac6911d5bff8282497488a05a514/kc-dev-flow/scripts/profile-contract-loader.py#L608).

## Reproduction

Use a valid disposable Pilot work item and the existing loader fixtures; do not alter an active task to reproduce this.

1. Bind a validation-stage pin with the normal `--work-item`, `--local-profile`, `--stage-pin`, `--stage-attempt` and `--write-stage-pin` arguments. Keep the plugin and accepted contract unchanged.
2. Append a Stage Report to the work item, then invoke the same loader and attempt without `--write-stage-pin`.
3. It refuses with `ACTIVE_STAGE_PIN_MISMATCH: restore the pinned plugin version and bytes`, although the plugin did not change. A different attempt string or `--accept-local-profile-refit` does not admit the continuation.
4. In a disposable fixture, project the declared feedback target from validation back to implementation while retaining the rejected validation pin. `bind_stage_pin` refuses with `STAGE_PIN_TRANSITION_MISMATCH: current stage is not the pinned next stage` because the normal next stage is done. This target-stage case was exercised in memory, not by changing live workflow state.

The actual installed read-only loader reproduced the first refusal. Six additional direct-function diagnostic cases used the real installed `bind_stage_pin`, without writing any pin or dispatching work:

| Case | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen-hash positive control in memory | accepted |
| Current append-only work record | ACTIVE_STAGE_PIN_MISMATCH |
| New attempt in the same stage | ACTIVE_STAGE_PIN_MISMATCH |
| Local-profile refit option | ACTIVE_STAGE_PIN_MISMATCH |
| Feedback target projected to implementation | STAGE_PIN_TRANSITION_MISMATCH |
| Hypothetical new pin, then another report append | ACTIVE_STAGE_PIN_MISMATCH |

All diagnostic assertions passed, meaning these behaviors were reproduced, not that continuation is correct. Loader, work item, local profile and pin hashes were unchanged afterward. No model, cloud run, product edit or real transition was performed.

## Expected outcome

Provide one supported correction-continuation path in the existing loader/dispatch contract:

- Distinguish report/progress updates from changes to accepted authority; do not simply ignore the work-item hash or assume every appended section is harmless.
- Accept an explicitly authorized feedback-to correction while binding it to the rejected revision, accepted repair scope and pinned contract. Preserve the old pin and rejection evidence.
- Continue to refuse unauthorized changes to goal, non-goals, acceptance criteria, package bytes, work-item identity or correction scope. A changed attempt name alone must not grant authority.
- Exercise the real loader and feedback handoff with regressions for report-only continuation, authorized repair, unauthorized scope drift and a second report after repair.

Please keep this separate from the affected PR-review product change. No new standing workflow, blanket bypass, or automatic approval of rejected work is requested. Source inspection has not established a Spacedock engine defect.

{"body":"## Problem

In a greenfield project using kc-dev-flow 4.1.1, the operator recommended Production based on the eventual goal of ongoing personal use, persistent state, and hosted deployment. The Captain understood the choice as establishing the project foundation. Work consequently prioritized hosted operations and recovery before proving the first real input-to-query journey.

This is primarily an operator selection and explanation error. `choose-work-profile` already asks whether credible negative evidence could change the next commitment, and recommends POC when it could. The improvement is to make that distinction concrete enough that a profile label cannot obscure the commitment being accepted.

## Suggested improvement

- Ground the recommendation in this work item's next commitment, unresolved assumption, and observable result, rather than the product's eventual lifespan or seriousness.
- Before selection, briefly show the concrete work included by the recommendation: project scaffolding, a disposable integrated experiment, limited real use, or an operated release with persistence/recovery responsibilities. A foundation task and an operational commitment are different choices.
- Show the smallest lower-commitment alternative and the specific evidence that makes it insufficient, when recommending Production while the first user journey is still unproved.
- Distinguish existing valued state/consumers from state the experiment might create. An empty repository alone should neither force POC nor justify Production.
- Keep this within the existing selection conversation. Do not add a separate approval stage, standing audit, or mandatory multi-profile pipeline.

## Expected behavior

For an unproved input/model integration, the operator can recommend a bounded POC with a real journey and a falsifier, while deferring future operating guarantees. For an explicit operated-release commitment or existing compatibility obligation, Production remains valid even in a new repository.

The Captain should be able to explain what will be delivered and which operational duties are being accepted before approving the profile. If the Captain understands the proposal as project scaffolding while the operator plans production operations, selection has not communicated the scope adequately.

## Scope

Review the selection wording/examples and its handoff to the committed profile receipt. Preserve existing work and truthful pending obligations when correcting a mistaken selection; do not retroactively relabel completed Production work as a successful POC. This issue is follow-up work for the maintainer, not a request to modify the plugin during the originating project.

{"body":"## Problem

During a greenfield project using kc-dev-flow 4.1.1, an integrated implementation and its reviews existed, but understanding the architecture still required reading code, a long work-item history, and several design notes. The repository had bound project context and a runnable README, yet lacked a clear architecture entry point for a reader returning to the project.

The current contracts require coherent project-context authority and maintenance when described claims change. They do not make the initial architecture coverage and discoverability requirement sufficiently explicit for a new project, particularly a POC whose implementation will be retained. This is also an operator documentation gap; the absence of a particular filename alone does not establish a contract violation.

## Proposed requirement

Require a discoverable architecture explanation proportional to the work, including POCs. Use `ARCHITECTURE.md` as the default for a new repository retaining implementation, while accepting an existing authoritative architecture section or document linked from the bound project-context entry point. Do not create a duplicate merely to satisfy the filename.

| Work | Minimum architecture explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Disposable POC | An outline in the Exploration Brief: components, data flow, external boundaries, and assumptions being tested. Keep unverified design explicitly tentative. |
| POC with retained implementation | A repository entry point explaining the retained components and responsibilities, inputs/outputs, persistence and source-of-truth boundaries, important package roles, and the code or commands that verify those claims. |
| Pilot / Production | Extend the same explanation with applicable authorization, deployment, failure, recovery, and compatibility boundaries. Do not require irrelevant sections. |

Identify the explanation's home before implementation; align retained documentation with the implementation before the existing implementation/validation boundary. A POC without a shape stage performs the small initial classification in build. Do not require a completed architecture before the experiment has answered its question.

## Preserve existing boundaries

- Keep one project-context authority; route to the deeper explanation from that authority.
- Keep proposed design, unresolved hypotheses, review history, deployment snapshots, and mutable progress in the work item or its planning authority. Retained architecture documents describe implemented behavior.
- Reuse project-context maintenance and retained-document policy for changes and validation. If a diagram is used, apply the existing render-and-check rule.
- Add no new workflow stage, approval gate, architecture reviewer, documentation generator, mandatory diagram tool, or parallel roadmap/status file.
- Do not reopen completed work or require a new file for a one-line change whose existing architecture explanation remains accurate.

## Acceptance examples

1. A new retained POC cannot exit with its architectural explanation discoverable only in a long execution log. A reader can follow the README to it and trace an input through processing, persistence, and query/output.
2. A disposable POC can complete with its small Exploration Brief outline and outcome; it is not required to build a permanent documentation set.
3. An existing repository with a linked architecture section satisfies the requirement without adding `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
4. A changed persistence or API boundary updates the authoritative explanation in the same delivery; checks cite the relevant code or runnable contract.
5. An unchanged existing explanation does not trigger boilerplate documentation edits or another review loop.

## Suggested scope

Review adoption/brief guidance and the selected profile's build/verification outputs together with `project-context-maintenance.md` and `retained-document-policy.md`. Reuse their existing authority and proportionality rules.

Related: #393 addresses explaining the next commitment during profile selection. This issue addresses architecture discoverability after that commitment is chosen. This is a maintainer follow-up proposal, not authorization to implement a plugin change or expand the originating product task.

{"body":"## Problem and accepted outcome

Relay PRs [#195](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/pull/195) and [#196](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/pull/196) passed through completion claims without an adequate comment-necessity pass. Both needed Captain-triggered cleanup; #196 also needed a second correction because shortened comments still described the runtime incorrectly.

Make the existing development route refuse completion when required comment-review evidence is missing or stale, and make its existing validation perspective inspect the actual changed comments. Preserve useful invariant, security, compatibility and rejected-alternative explanations. A smaller comment count is diagnostic, never the success criterion.

**Handoff authority:** Kent requested: “先把完整計劃與案例開到 plugin repo，等於交接給那邊的 agent，然後你繼續 relay 的工作，不要在這裡分心”. This issue hands planning and implementation to the plugin-repository agent. The Relay agent will not implement this plugin change. Follow this repository's own admission/profile and delivery authority; this issue does not select a profile, authorize merging, or claim implementation is complete.

## Current evidence and ownership

Incident environment: installed `kc-dev-flow` 4.1.1 and Spacedock 0.27.2. The installed kernel already required comparison of added files, dependencies, abstractions, tests and comments; cut/kept comment candidates with reasons; and goal sufficiency plus minimal necessity for the same candidate. Pilot build/verify required-output bullets did not explicitly carry that comment evidence. Loading these rules was mistaken for discharging them. Green CI and a functional review did not expose the omission.

Rechecked plugin main at `c2c62bf9dff5c3af1e27eb643a15eadf9023485f`: [kernel](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/c2c62bf9dff5c3af1e27eb643a15eadf9023485f/kc-dev-flow/references/kernel.md) still contains the comment-necessity rule and completion invariant. Main now also says removals are graded by minimal necessity. Re-read current contracts before editing; do not assume the installed incident version equals the target source.

Canonical output/proof policy belongs to kc-dev-flow. Runtime transitions belong to Spacedock. Trace the actual completion caller before choosing files. Extend the existing result and completion path; if a Spacedock adapter change is necessary, name the smallest external dependency explicitly. Do not call a prose-only instruction or an unused checker enforcement.

A discovery warning: Relay's Local Profile claims a `surface-map-check.py` exists, but that script was absent at the activated 4.1.1 package's `scripts/` path. Do not depend on that declaration or an old memory as executable evidence; verify the live target package. This is context, not authorization to absorb a general adoption refit.

## Proposed implementation: three existing boundaries

1. **Implementation exit:** report the reviewed base/candidate and relevant changed-comment locations in the existing stage output. Record cut/shortened candidates and retained candidates with concrete reasons. A retained reason answers what a maintainer would misunderstand without the comment. Cover the changed region rather than a token example. A legitimate no-comment-change case must be supported by the actual diff. Do not create a parallel receipt system or a per-line essay.
2. **Existing validation:** inspect the actual comments and nearby implementation at that candidate. Verify the claimed dispositions, including retained factual claims and necessary explanations. Do not accept an author's “reviewed”, “all necessary”, or smaller line count as proof. Use the existing reviewer when the route has one; retain lighter profiles' proportional depth and direct-proof route. Do not add a reviewer or stage to every task.
3. **Existing completion decision:** refuse missing, malformed, contradictory, or stale required evidence before advancing/completing through the supported route. The same result can name the missing item and return repair work to the owner. Mechanical checks can establish presence, applicability and revision binding; semantic judgment establishes usefulness and truth. Explicitly document this boundary and any raw-runtime bypass instead of claiming tamper resistance.

Resolve the kernel's existing “no receipt or commentary when no scope drift” wording consistently with its comment-pass requirement. Reuse existing output. Avoid duplicate policy across kernel, profiles, prompts and repository mods.

## Case corpus with fixed revisions

Use immutable Git objects, not the present PR diff: both PRs merged on 2026-09-10 and #196 was rebased before merge. Keep original and corrected pairs on their matching historical base. Fetch missing objects from the Relay repository; a missing object is an unavailable fixture, not permission to substitute HEAD.

### PR #195: test discovery excludes nested worktrees

- Before the PR: `ab0db32cacfb3dc2a26508a5a3dd9091f5353b97`.
- Original candidate: `d05ab4962621d2eaebc63cd53999f855d5eb2c0e`.
- Comment correction/final PR head: `2a959700265cd1f36fd4bf606142fb4395be735b`.
- Files: `.gitignore`, `biome.json`, `netlify/lib/operator.test.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`. Cleanup touches three; `biome.json` is unchanged by cleanup.
- Original comments repeat failure history in Git ignore rules, the operator scan and Vitest config, including historical test counts and a date. Examples: “15,679 tests instead of 786”; “since 2026-08-14”; four lines beside the new `.context` exclusion restating what the walk does.
- Correction removes that history and condenses an existing long config explanation. Retained facts: Vitest does not use `.gitignore`; Playwright owns `test/browser/**` specs.
- Observed correction: +2/-25 lines, net -23. TypeScript output with comments and source maps removed is identical for the two TS files; non-comment Git ignore patterns are identical. Five operator tests and explicit two-file Biome check passed. CI run [34457930914](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/actions/runs/34457930914) passed its selected jobs.
- Important limit: this proves this cleanup preserved behavior. It is not a completed whole-PR necessity proof for every exclusion, and it is not an automated comment-review result. The original PR body said “without-it unanswered: None”; that sentence is not evidence.

### PR #196: packages carrying multiple artifacts

- Historical delivery base: `d05ab4962621d2eaebc63cd53999f855d5eb2c0e`.
- Original fully implemented candidate before comment cleanup: `a71a73dca40459451d49d44113e20167ad1998f0`.
- First cleanup: `1169ef08100364cc61f78d7b4554f6ab3a04262d`.
- Corrected semantic comment follow-up: `8db0432e2f67ffb2b025cf3aba716553029f9509`.
- Rebased final PR head: `7a78a3164af1074bf8c9fc0b4a849e64cff165cd`; squash merge `c5ad86603652d199affdfd454cbcbdc339dd95f2`. These later hashes include a different base; do not use a cross-base aggregate diff to label comment-only changes.
- Six original PR files: `docs/architecture.md`, `netlify/lib/manifest.ts`, `manifest.test.ts`, `room-feedback.ts`, `room-feedback.test.ts`, `room-view.ts` (the last five under `netlify/lib/`).
- Cut candidates: three adjacent docblocks above `briefingArtifactCount`, two describing other functions; signature translations; repeated stored-identity explanations; repair narratives in tests; an architecture-limit row's historical explanation.
- Keep candidates: collision-work bound, case-folding filesystem overwrite risk, file/directory incompatibility, stored-identity trust boundary, one Result carrying one artifact identity, compatibility for one-artifact packages, bounded target parsing. Removing these useful reasons just to hit a quota is a failure.
- **Essential semantic negative case:** first cleanup still implied malformed/oversized result errors always belong to later submission validation. For a multi-artifact package, unresolved target instead reaches a 404 before that validator. Independent validation caught this. Final text is “Bound target parsing independently of later submission validation.” The catch comment was removed. This case distinguishes factual review from counting comments or checking report fields.
- Observed cleanup: first +11/-111, then +1/-2; net -101 lines across both. Added production comment lines dropped 66 to 7 (diagnostic only). Five TS files had identical emitted JavaScript versus the original. The equivalence instrument rejected an in-memory cap mutation from 256 to 1.
- Existing product evidence: 140 focused tests; same real-handler journey fails two-file publish on historical base and succeeds on corrected candidate, including byte readback and feedback identity. Persistence uses a fake store: no real Blobs, hosted UI or deployment claim. Final corrected-candidate CI: [34456223902](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/actions/runs/34456223902).
- Durable detailed case material: [cut/kept and necessity evidence](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/blob/53d697233f934df8b0a8f4261a43f95305fe0f66/a-package-can-carry-a-folder/folder-correction-evidence.md), [independent validation output](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/subspace-relay/blob/53d697233f934df8b0a8f4261a43f95305fe0f66/a-package-can-carry-a-folder/folder-validation-evidence.txt). These links refer to the separate state branch's immutable commit, not product main.

## Experiment and refusal matrix

Freeze baseline and proposed plugin commits, corpus objects, model, reasoning setting, ordinary task prompt, available tools and context budget before measuring. The treatment is the three-boundary change, not a more suggestive user prompt. Use fresh contexts for baseline and treatment and keep correction diffs, historical verdicts, expected answers and this issue's answer key out of reviewer inputs. Capture actual reviewed revisions, outputs, completion decisions, failures, elapsed time and token/cost data when observable; mark unavailable measurements honestly. Separate deterministic tests from model runs; one model run is not a reliability estimate.

| Input / intervention | Expected result | Evidence type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Comment-changing diff; omit comment-review evidence | Completion refuses and names omission | Deterministic boundary invocation |
| Evidence belongs to earlier candidate, different base or another task | Refusal before advance/completion | Deterministic binding test |
| Author says only “reviewed”, “all necessary”, or “None” | No clean semantic verdict; incomplete evidence or reviewer rejection | Structural refusal plus semantic review as applicable |
| PR #195 original narrative comments | Reviewer identifies concrete unnecessary blocks, preserves tool-ownership reasons | Fresh-context semantic run |
| PR #196 original misplaced/repeated docblocks | Reviewer identifies location/content defects and useful invariants | Fresh-context semantic run |
| PR #196 first cleanup with false downstream-error ownership | Reviewer flags the actual 404 control-flow counterexample | Semantic negative control |
| Corrected pair with truthful, complete evidence | Supported route accepts without unrelated ceremony | Positive control |
| Diff with no relevant comment change | Supported route proceeds without a fabricated cut/keep essay | Applicability control |
| Remove useful trust-boundary/compatibility explanation solely to shrink text | Reviewer rejects unjustified removal | Preservation control |
| Disable the newly integrated completion check | Missing/stale-evidence test now fails | Mutation proves the check is on the execution path |

Run baseline and treatment on the same frozen cases. Report discrepancies, missed defects and false positives, not just pass totals. If baseline already catches a case, that case shows preservation rather than measured improvement. Expect known-case regression evidence; do not claim generalization from two cases whose answers designed the fix. After freezing the implementation, select an additional PR not used for design and not already visible to its reviewer as a holdout. Define its rubric before the run. A holdout improves confidence but does not prove universal reliability.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Identify and exercise the actual implementation-output, validation and completion call sites; prose/unused helpers alone do not qualify.
- [ ] AC-2: Missing/stale evidence refuses on the real supported completion path; disabling that integration makes its negative test fail.
- [ ] AC-3: Blind case runs produce concrete cut/keep reasons, detect the #196 false-error-ownership case, and preserve necessary explanations; record misses and false positives.
- [ ] AC-4: Corrected and no-comment controls proceed at their existing profile depth; no new global stage, recurring reviewer, quota or parallel receipt/tracker.
- [ ] AC-5: Report frozen baseline/treatment/corpus/model identities and observed results, separating deterministic enforcement, model quality, behavioral equivalence, and generalization claims.
- [ ] AC-6: A holdout is evaluated only after the implementation/rubric freezes, or the outcome is explicitly limited to known-case regression pending holdout.
- [ ] AC-7: Run repository-required package checks and document any adapter dependency; finish at a reviewable PR with risks and remaining decisions. No merge/release claim.

## Boundaries and stopping condition

No Relay product changes, user-worktree mutations, new Relay CI lane, comment-density threshold, broad cleanup of historical PRs, generic without-it harness, new review service, or workflow-wide policy refit. Do not edit installed plugin caches. Reuse existing stage output and supported transition mechanism. A comment's necessity concerns information preserved for maintainers; unchanged runtime output cannot establish that necessity by itself.
